articles.title: Relax, Balance, Uplift: Reading Indica, Sativa and Hybrid Labels
articles.metaTitle: Indica, Sativa or Hybrid? | Humboldt's Premium Arcata
articles.description: What indica, sativa and hybrid labels really tell you, why terpenes matter, and how to use our Relax, Balance and Uplift guide at our Arcata dispensary.
articles.dek: The old labels are a fine place to start, as long as you know what they can and can't tell you.
articles.body:
## Three words you'll see everywhere

Walk into almost any dispensary, ours included, and you'll find flower sorted three ways: indica, sativa and hybrid. They're the oldest labels in cannabis, and shoppers have leaned on them for decades. They're a fine place to start. They're just not the whole story.

Here's the traditional shorthand:

- **Indica** is linked with a heavier, settle-in feel. People often reach for it at the end of the day.
- **Sativa** is linked with a lighter, more upbeat feel. People often reach for it earlier in the day.
- **Hybrid** is a cross of the two. Most cultivars on shelves today are some kind of hybrid.

On our menu you'll see these labels as categories ([indica](/a-indica-flower/), [sativa](/a-sativa-flower/) and [hybrid](/a-hybrid-flower/)) and as short tags in many product names, like (I), (S) or (H).

## Relax, Balance, Uplift

To make browsing easier, we group things by feel:

1. **Relax** points to indica.
2. **Balance** points to hybrid.
3. **Uplift** points to sativa.

Think of it as a loose guide, not a promise. Two people can try the same cultivar and describe it in completely different ways. Your mood, your setting, how much you take and how often you use cannabis all play a part.

## Why the label isn't the whole story

The words indica and sativa started out describing plants: their shape, their leaves and where they came from. After generations of crossbreeding, most of what's on shelves today is a mix. The name on the jar tells you a little about a plant's family tree. It tells you less about how it will feel.

Two other things on the label tend to tell you more.

### Cannabinoids

These are the active compounds in the plant. **THC** is the one that causes the high. **CBD** doesn't produce a high the way THC does, and some products pair the two. On flower labels you may also see **THCA**, the raw form of THC that converts to THC when heated.

A higher THC number means more THC, but it doesn't predict whether you'll enjoy something. Plenty of people prefer a lower-THC flower they love over the biggest number on the menu.

### Terpenes

Terpenes are the aromatic compounds that give cannabis its smell. They're the same family of compounds you find in citrus peel, pine needles and lavender. Many growers and shoppers believe terpenes help shape the experience along with the cannabinoids. The research is still young, so treat any terpene chart as a hint, not a rule.

A few you'll hear about:

- **Myrcene**: earthy and musky, also found in hops and mango.
- **Limonene**: bright citrus.
- **Caryophyllene**: peppery and spicy, also found in black pepper.
- **Pinene**: fresh pine.
- **Linalool**: soft and floral, like lavender.

The simplest test is your nose. If you love the smell of a cultivar, that's useful information.

## How to shop by feel

- **Start with the feeling you're after,** then use Relax, Balance or Uplift to narrow things down.
- **Ask about terpenes.** A budtender can help you compare the aroma and profile of a few options.
- **Take notes.** Jot down what you tried, how much and how it felt. Over time, your own notes beat any label.
- **Go easy with anything new.** Start with a small amount and give it time.

Everyone responds to cannabis differently, and the same product can feel different from one day to the next. If you have health questions, talk with your doctor. For everything else, come see us at 460 I St. We're happy to help you find something that fits the evening you have in mind.
takeaways: Indica, sativa and hybrid are traditional labels: a starting point, not a promise.
Terpenes, cannabinoids and your own body usually tell you more than the label.
Use Relax, Balance and Uplift as a loose guide, and start small with anything new.

articles.title: Flower to Topicals: Every Format on Our Menu
articles.metaTitle: A Guide to Cannabis Formats | Humboldt's Premium Arcata
articles.description: Flower, prerolls, carts, AIOs, concentrates, edibles, drinks, tinctures, topicals and CBD: a plain guide to every format at Humboldt's Premium Arcata.
articles.dek: A quick, plain tour of every way cannabis shows up on our menu, and where to find each one.
articles.body:
## Start here

Cannabis comes in a lot of shapes now, and the menu can feel like a lot the first time you scroll it. Here's a plain walk through every format we carry: what it is and where to find it. Effects vary by person and product, so whatever you choose, start small and give it time.

## Flower

Flower is the dried, cured bud of the plant, the classic. You can grind it and smoke it in a pipe or a joint, or use a dry herb vaporizer. Many of our flower listings tell you how it was grown (sungrown, mixed light or indoor) and its type (indica, sativa or hybrid). Sizes run from eighths to quarters, half ounces and full ounces.

[Shop all flower](/a-all-flower-1/), or go straight to [indica](/a-indica-flower/), [sativa](/a-sativa-flower/), [hybrid](/a-hybrid-flower/) or [Humboldt Grown](/a-humboldt-grown/).

## Prerolls

A preroll is flower that comes already rolled and ready to light. You'll find singles, multipacks and blunts. **Infused prerolls** add concentrate inside or on the outside, which makes them much stronger than a regular joint. If you're new, start with a plain preroll and take it slow.

[Shop prerolls](/a-prerolls/)

## Cartridges and AIOs

Vape cartridges hold cannabis oil and screw onto a battery. Most use the standard **510 thread**, so they fit most 510 batteries. An **AIO** (all-in-one) has the battery built in, so there's nothing to match up. You'll also see pods, which click into their own brand's battery. Oils come in several styles, including live resin and live rosin.

[Shop cartridges](/a-cartridges/), and find batteries in [accessories](/accessories/).

## Concentrates

Concentrates are the plant's resin, separated from the plant material. They're strong, so a little goes a long way. Most are dabbed (vaporized on a hot surface) or added to a bowl or joint. Names you'll see:

- **Live resin**: made from plants frozen fresh at harvest instead of dried, to keep more of the fresh aroma.
- **Badder**: whipped and creamy, a bit like cake frosting.
- **Sauce**: runny and aromatic, often with crystals in it.
- **Diamonds**: crystals of THCA, often sold with sauce.
- **Rosin**: pressed out with heat and pressure, with no solvents.
- **Dry sift**: a traditional hash made by sifting resin from dried flower through fine screens.

You'll also see shatter, sugar and crumble, named for their textures, plus RSO tablets. Those tablets list their milligrams per piece, and many carry far more THC than a typical gummy.

[Shop concentrates](/a-concentrates/)

## Edibles

Edibles are cannabis you eat: gummies, chews, mints and chocolates. They take longer to kick in than smoking, and they last longer. Read the label for milligrams per piece, start low and wait at least 2 hours before taking more.

[Shop edibles](/edibles/)

## Drinks

Cannabis drinks include sodas, teas, seltzers, lemonades and shots. A lot of people feel a drink sooner than a gummy. Check the label: some drinks hold 10 mg in the whole can, while others hold 100 mg, which is several servings.

[Shop drinks](/a-drinks/)

## Tinctures

Tinctures are liquid extracts in a dropper bottle. You measure a few drops at a time, which makes it easy to adjust slowly. Some pair CBD with a little THC, so check the ratio on the label.

[Shop tinctures](/a-tintctures/)

## Topicals

Topicals are balms, lotions and patches that go on your skin. Balms and lotions aren't generally known for producing a high. Transdermal products are different: they're designed to move cannabinoids through the skin, so read those labels closely.

[Shop topicals](/a-topicals/)

## CBD and CBN

CBD and CBN are cannabinoids other than THC. On our menu they show up in gummies, tinctures, topicals, carts and drinks, and many of those products contain THC too. Look for the ratio on the label, like 1:1 or 30:1.

[Shop CBD and CBN](/a-cbd-cbn/)

## Not sure where to start?

Ask us. Tell a budtender what kind of experience you're after and how much cannabis you've used before, and we'll walk you through a few options. You can browse everything on the [shop page](/shop/), and the [sale items](/a-sale-items/) are worth a look.
takeaways: Flower and prerolls are the classics; infused prerolls and concentrates are much stronger.
Carts screw onto a battery, while AIOs have one built in.
Edibles, drinks and tinctures are measured in milligrams, so read the label and start low.

articles.title: Edibles and Drinks: Start Low, Go Slow
articles.metaTitle: Edibles and Drinks Guide | Humboldt's Premium Arcata
articles.description: New to edibles or THC drinks? How to read mg labels, why drinks can feel sooner, how long effects last, and how to store them away from kids and pets.
articles.dek: Edibles and drinks are easy to enjoy and easy to overdo, so here's how to read the label and pace yourself.
articles.body:
## The one rule

If you remember one thing, make it this: start low, go slow. Edibles and drinks are an easy, smoke-free way to enjoy cannabis, but they work differently than smoking. The most common mistake is taking more before the first dose has kicked in.

## Why edibles take their time

When you smoke or vape, you usually feel it within minutes. When you eat cannabis, it goes through your digestive system first, and that takes a while. Edibles can take anywhere from 30 minutes to 2 hours to kick in, and the effects can last several hours.

Lots of things change the timing: your body, what you've eaten, the product itself and how often you use cannabis. Two people can eat the same gummy and have very different evenings.

## Drinks often feel sooner

Many people find that cannabis drinks kick in sooner than a classic edible. Sooner isn't the same as instant, though, and a drink is still measured in milligrams like any edible. Sip slowly, set the can down for a while and see how you feel before you open another. It's also smart to skip the alcohol when you're enjoying a cannabis drink.

## Reading the milligram label

Every edible and drink lists its THC in milligrams (mg). Look for two numbers:

1. **Total mg in the package.** This is usually the big number on the front.
2. **Mg per piece or per serving.** This is the amount you actually take.

Do the quick math. A 20-piece pack labeled 100 mg works out to 5 mg a piece. A 10-piece pack labeled 100 mg is 10 mg a piece. Drinks vary a lot: on our menu, some hold 10 mg in the whole can, while others hold 100 mg, which is several servings. Some products also list CBD, CBN or other cannabinoids with a ratio like 1:1.

A few products carry much more per piece. Some concentrate tablets list 25 mg, 50 mg or even 100 mg each. Those aren't a first-timer's product.

## A simple first-time plan

- **Start small.** Many first-timers start around 2.5 to 5 mg of THC. Half a piece is a perfectly good start.
- **Wait at least 2 hours** before taking more. Set a timer if it helps.
- **Pick a relaxed setting** with nothing important on the schedule, and don't drive.
- **Keep notes.** Write down what you took, how much and when, so next time is easier.

If you feel too high, find a calm, comfortable spot, sip some water and give it time. If you're ever worried about yourself or someone else, call 911.

## Storing edibles and drinks safely

Edibles and drinks can look just like regular candy and soda, so safe storage matters.

- Keep them in their original child-resistant packaging.
- Store them up high, locked if you can, away from kids and pets.
- Give cannabis drinks their own spot in the fridge, away from regular sodas.
- Keep the label so you always know what's inside and how strong it is.

If a child gets into cannabis, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222. If a pet does, call your vet. In an emergency, call 911.

## Enjoying them in our courtyard

Our courtyard welcomes edibles and THC drinks today. If you'd like to enjoy something out back, give it time to kick in, pace yourself and plan your ride home before you start: a sober driver, a walk or a ride. Read up on [courtyard manners](/learn/courtyard-etiquette/) before you head out back, and browse [edibles](/edibles/) and [drinks](/a-drinks/) anytime.
takeaways: Many first-timers start around 2.5 to 5 mg of THC and wait at least 2 hours before taking more.
Drinks often feel sooner than edibles, but read the mg label either way.
Store edibles and drinks in child-resistant packaging, away from kids and pets.

articles.title: Your First Visit to Humboldt's Premium Arcata
articles.metaTitle: Your First Visit in Arcata | Humboldt's Premium Arcata
articles.description: Planning your first visit to Humboldt's Premium at 460 I St in Arcata? What to bring, how to pay, ordering ahead, the courtyard and our exchange policy.
articles.dek: Everything you need for an easy first trip to our shop on the corner of I St. and Samoa Blvd.
articles.body:
## Welcome in

Come in, shop the store or just say hi to everyone. That's the whole idea. Humboldt's Premium Arcata sits at 460 I St, on the corner of I St. and Samoa Blvd., just north of the Arcata Marsh. If the building looks familiar, it used to be the V&N Burger Bar. James, a professional contractor, built the store with a layout inspired by the TV show Bar Rescue and designed from the customer's point of view. Look for the bright slat walls and the lights floating from the ceiling.

Here's what to know before you stop by.

## Bring a valid ID

You need to be 21 or older, and ID is required for every sale. No ID, no sale. Bring a valid government-issued photo ID. Medical patients 18 and over need a physician's recommendation, so if that's you, call us at 707-630-4098 before your visit and we'll tell you what to bring.

## How to pay

We take cash and debit. Debit has a $3.00 fee. Sorry, no credit. All sales include excise and sales tax.

## Order ahead if you like

You can place an order online from our [Shop](/shop/) page, or call it in at 707-630-4098, then come in to pick it up. It's handy when you already know what you want.

## What our budtenders can help with

Not sure what you're after? That's what we're here for. A budtender can:

- Walk you through the formats, from flower and prerolls to edibles, drinks and tinctures.
- Explain the label: THC and CBD numbers, milligrams and terpenes.
- Help you compare a few options based on the experience you're looking for.
- Point out the day's deals.

We're not doctors, so for health questions, check with yours. You can also read up ahead of time with our guides to [indica, sativa and hybrid](/learn/indica-sativa-hybrid/) and [every format on the menu](/learn/cannabis-formats/).

## Deals worth knowing

There are deals every day of the week, and on the 1st of every month, spending $50 or more gets you a spin of the wheel, while supplies last. See what's on at [Deals](/deals/). One thing to know: discounts cannot be stacked or applied to items on special or to sale items.

## The courtyard out back

Out back is our courtyard, with covered gazebos, fireplaces, patio heaters and a built-in rock waterfall (say hi to the Bigfoot statue on the rocks). Today it welcomes edibles and THC drinks. On November 10, 2026, the Arcata Planning Commission approved an outdoor smoking lounge on the patio for products bought in the store. The opening date and house rules will be posted by the store when they're set. Read more about the [courtyard lounge](/courtyard-lounge/).

## Our exchange policy

Please read this before you buy. Our policy reads: "No refunds on any purchase. No exchanges after 72 hrs. from purchase, must have original product and packaging from purchase for exchange. Exchanges for defective/damaged products will be for same products only. Certain restrictions apply." If you have a question about a purchase, call us at 707-630-4098.

## Plan your visit

Our posted hours are 9 am to 9 pm Monday through Saturday, and 10 am to 7 pm on Sunday. Check our [Visit page](/arcata-details/) for the latest hours and a map before a special trip. See you soon.
takeaways: Bring a valid government ID: 21 and over, or 18 and over with a physician's recommendation.
We take cash and debit ($3.00 debit fee). Sorry, no credit.
Order ahead online or by phone at 707-630-4098, then pick up in store.

articles.title: Courtyard Manners: What to Expect in Arcata's Backyard
articles.description: What to expect in our Arcata courtyard: edibles and THC drinks today, the newly approved smoking lounge, and good manners that keep it calm and clean.
articles.dek: Our courtyard is a calm, clean place to slow down, and a few good habits keep it that way for everyone.
articles.body:
## Arcata's backyard

Behind the shop is our courtyard. Look for the sunburst sign over the gate. Inside you'll find covered gazebos, fireplaces and a fire table, patio heaters for foggy nights, teal-cushioned wicker sofas and teak tables, and a built-in rock waterfall with a Bigfoot statue keeping watch. Jolly Giant Creek runs beside the lot, and the Arcata Marsh is just to the south. It's a nice place to sit for a minute before a walk at the Marsh.

Here's what to expect out back, plus a few good manners that keep it calm and clean for everyone.

## What's welcome today

Today the courtyard welcomes **edibles and THC drinks**. It's a non-smoking space for now, so please don't light up or vape out back.

## The smoking lounge is on its way

In April 2026, the Arcata City Council legalized on-site smoking. On November 10, 2026, the Arcata Planning Commission unanimously approved an outdoor smoking lounge on our patio, for products bought in the store. The lounge was pitched as calm and clean: daily litter sweeps, an air scrubber and a mellow feel, more like eating outside at a restaurant than a party.

There's no published opening date yet. The store will post the final house rules, and those rules will be the last word. Until then, think of this page as a friendly preview.

## Good courtyard manners

### Enjoy what you buy here

The city's approval covers products bought in the store. Plan on enjoying what you pick up inside, and ask a budtender if you're not sure what's welcome out back.

### Pace yourself

Edibles and drinks take time to kick in. Start low, go slow and give the first one a real chance before you reach for another. Our [edibles and drinks guide](/learn/edibles-and-drinks/) has the details.

### Keep it calm

Talk at a normal volume, share the good seats and give the people around you some room. Everyone's out there to unwind.

### Leave no trace

Pack out what you bring in, and leave your table the way you found it. With a creek right next door and the Marsh down the road, every wrapper and can should end up in the trash, not the water.

### Keep it in the courtyard

Consuming cannabis in public places is against California law. Please keep it in the courtyard, not on the sidewalk, in the parking lot or in your car.

### Respect the neighbors

We share this corner of Arcata with neighbors. Keep it quiet as you head out, and don't linger in the lot.

### Mind the fire

The fireplaces and heaters keep things cozy when the fog rolls in. Give them room, and keep jackets and bags clear.

### Plan your ride

Decide how you're getting home before you start. Designate a sober driver, walk or catch a ride. Never drive impaired, and keep your purchases sealed or in the trunk while you drive.

## Food and good company

Local food trucks, like Humboldt's own Fry Burger, park on site from time to time. We don't post a schedule, so ask us what's coming up.

Questions about the courtyard? Call us at 707-630-4098, or read more on the [courtyard lounge](/courtyard-lounge/) page.
takeaways: Today the courtyard welcomes edibles and THC drinks, and it's non-smoking for now.
The smoking lounge was approved Nov 10, 2026; the store will post the opening date and house rules.
Enjoy products bought in the store, leave no trace and plan a safe ride home.

articles.title: CBD and CBN: What They Are and How They Differ From THC
articles.metaTitle: CBD and CBN Explained | Humboldt's Premium Arcata
articles.description: A plain guide to CBD and CBN: what they are, how they're sold, how they differ from THC and how to read ratio labels like 1:1, from Humboldt's Premium.
articles.dek: CBD and CBN show up all over the menu, so here's what they are, how they're sold and what to look for on the label.
articles.body:
## More than one cannabinoid

The cannabis plant makes more than a hundred compounds called cannabinoids. THC is the famous one, the one that causes the high. CBD and CBN are two others you'll see on more and more labels. Here's a plain look at each, without the hype.

## What is CBD?

CBD, short for cannabidiol, is one of the best-known cannabinoids after THC. It doesn't produce a high the way THC does. Some people choose CBD-forward products, and many products pair CBD with THC.

Researchers are still learning what CBD does and doesn't do, and the claims you'll hear about it range from careful to wild. We'll stay on the careful side: we can tell you what's in a product, but not what it will do for you. If you have health questions, or you take any medication, talk with your doctor first.

## What is CBN?

CBN, short for cannabinol, forms as THC ages and breaks down. The plant has only small amounts of it, so products that feature CBN usually have it added. You'll often see CBN in products with evening or sleep-themed names. Those names are marketing, research on CBN is still limited, and effects vary by person and product.

## How they differ from THC

- **THC** is the compound that causes the high.
- **CBD** doesn't produce a high the way THC does.
- **CBN** is usually sold alongside THC, and research on how it feels on its own is still limited.

The big point: a product that features CBD or CBN can still contain plenty of THC. On our menu, most of them do. Treat a CBD or CBN product with THC in it the same way you'd treat any THC product.

## How they're usually sold

CBD and CBN show up in a lot of formats on our menu:

- **Gummies and chews**, often with ratios like 1:1 THC to CBD or THC to CBN.
- **Tinctures**, dropper bottles that pair CBD with a little THC.
- **Topicals**, including transdermal patches.
- **Cartridges** with high-CBD or 1:1 oils.
- **Drinks** that add a little CBD to the THC.

You'll also spot other minor cannabinoids on labels, like CBG and THCV. Find them in our [CBD and CBN](/a-cbd-cbn/), [tinctures](/a-tintctures/) and [topicals](/a-topicals/) categories, plus [edibles](/edibles/).

## Reading a ratio label

Ratios tell you how the cannabinoids compare. The order matters, so check the label to see which one comes first.

- **1:1** means equal parts, for example 50 mg of THC and 50 mg of CBD in a pack.
- **A big first number**, like 30:1 CBD to THC, means mostly CBD with a little THC.
- **Three-part ratios**, like 20:5:2, list three cannabinoids. The label tells you which is which.

Then look at the milligrams per piece or per serving. The ratio tells you the balance, and the milligrams tell you the amount.

## A few tips

- Start low and go slow, even with CBD-forward products, since many contain THC.
- Read the whole label: total mg, mg per piece and the ratio.
- Ask a budtender to point out products that match what you're looking for.
- Store everything safely, away from kids and pets.

We're happy to walk you through the CBD and CBN shelf next time you're in.
takeaways: CBD doesn't produce a high the way THC does, and research on CBN is still limited.
Many CBD and CBN products on our menu also contain THC, so read the ratio and the mg.
We can tell you what's in a product, not what it will do for you; ask your doctor about health questions.

articles.title: Why Humboldt Grown Matters
articles.metaTitle: Why Humboldt Grown Matters | Humboldt's Premium Arcata
articles.description: Why Humboldt-grown cannabis matters: Emerald Triangle heritage, sun-grown vs mixed light vs indoor, and how to shop local farms at our Arcata store.
articles.dek: Humboldt has been growing cannabis for generations, and buying local keeps that story going.
articles.body:
## A long growing story

Humboldt County is one corner of the Emerald Triangle, along with Mendocino and Trinity counties, a region famous for cannabis. Many of the region's growers trace their roots to the back-to-the-land families who settled these hills in the 1960s and 1970s. They learned to grow among the redwoods, rivers and coastal fog, and passed that know-how down through generations.

Since California legalized adult-use cannabis, licensed farms here can sell through licensed shops like ours, so buying local is easy and legal.

## Our own roots

Humboldt's Premium is family-run. James Alves, a professional contractor, and his wife Amy turned to cannabis when construction slowed after the real estate crash. They started with a collective, then a farm, Humboldt AF Cannabis, then delivery services and, later, the stores in Eureka and Arcata. In the company's own words: "Humboldt AF Cannabis is a farm to table Cannabis company."

## Sun-grown, mixed light and indoor

Many flower listings on our menu tell you how the plants were grown. Here's what those words mean.

### Sun-grown

Grown outdoors under the sun, with no artificial light. Outdoor plants usually get one harvest a year, in the fall. Using the sun instead of grow lights takes far less electricity, and plenty of people love the character of a good outdoor crop.

### Mixed light

Grown in a greenhouse or hoop house that uses the sun plus some help: blackout covers to shorten the day, extra lights or both. That control lets farmers time their harvests, often more than once a year.

### Indoor

Grown entirely under lights in a controlled room, where farmers manage light, temperature and humidity all year. Many shoppers like indoor flower for its look and consistency.

None of these is automatically better. They're just different, and the best way to find your favorite is to try a few side by side.

## Why buying local matters

- **It supports local farms.** Money spent on Humboldt-grown cannabis helps keep local growers going.
- **It keeps a heritage alive.** Generations of growing know-how live in these hills.
- **It travels less.** Cannabis grown here has a short trip to our shelves.

We give back too, donating to parks and recreation programs, including the FFA.

## Reading a Humboldt Grown listing

Our menu names pack in a lot of information. A typical flower listing tells you:

- **Who made it**: the farm or brand name usually comes first.
- **How it was grown**: sungrown, mixed light or indoor.
- **The cultivar and type**: the variety name, often with a tag like (I), (S) or (H).
- **Potency and size**: the THC percentage and the weight, like 3.5g for an eighth.

## Shop our Humboldt Grown category

We keep a dedicated [Humboldt Grown](/a-humboldt-grown/) category for flower and prerolls. Names you might see there include our own Humboldt Premium Cannabis line (sungrown and indoor eighths, plus 707 Rolls prerolls), alongside Willow Creekside Farms, Sunrise Mountain Farms, Humboldt Homegrown, Humboldt Genetics and Widowmaker. Stock changes daily, so check the live menu for what's in today.

Not sure where to start? Ask a budtender to help you compare a sungrown eighth and an indoor eighth. It's an easy way to learn what you like. You can also browse [all flower](/a-all-flower-1/) and [prerolls](/a-prerolls/).
takeaways: Humboldt is part of the Emerald Triangle, with generations of growing know-how.
Sun-grown, mixed light and indoor describe how a plant was grown, not which is best.
Our Humboldt Grown category makes it easy to shop local flower and prerolls.

articles.title: California Cannabis Laws, in Plain English
articles.metaTitle: California Cannabis Laws | Humboldt's Premium Arcata
articles.description: California cannabis laws in plain English: who can buy, how much you can carry, where you can consume, driving rules and what's new in Arcata for 2026.
articles.dek: A plain summary of California's cannabis rules, plus what's new in Arcata, with a link to the official source.
articles.body:
## The short version

Cannabis is legal for adults in California, with rules. This page is a plain summary of the main state rules as of 2026, written by a neighborhood shop, not a law firm, so please don't treat it as legal advice. For the official word, visit the [Department of Cannabis Control](https://cannabis.ca.gov/), and remember that cities and counties can add rules of their own.

## Who can buy

- **Adults 21 and over** can buy from a licensed retailer.
- **Medical patients 18 and over** need a physician's recommendation.
- **A valid government ID is required.** At our shop it's simple: no ID, no sale.

## How much you can carry

Adults 21 and over may buy and possess up to:

- **28.5 grams of non-concentrated cannabis**, like flower. That's about an ounce.
- **8 grams of concentrated cannabis**, like dabs and other extracts.

## Where you can consume

Consuming cannabis in public places is illegal. That includes sidewalks, parks, beaches and trails, the Marsh included. The exception is a licensed on-site consumption area that the city allows, like a dispensary lounge. Home is the usual spot, and landlords and property owners can set their own rules.

## On the road

- **Never drive impaired.** Driving under the influence of cannabis is illegal and dangerous.
- **Keep it sealed.** While driving, keep cannabis in a sealed container or in the trunk.
- **Plan ahead.** Designate a sober driver, walk or catch a ride.

## State lines

Don't take cannabis across state lines, even into another state where it's legal. Federal law still treats cannabis differently than California does.

## Growing at home

Adults 21 and over may grow up to six plants at home. The state limit is six living plants per residence, not per person, and local rules apply, so check with your city or county before you plant.

## What's new in Arcata

Arcata has been busy. In April 2026, the Arcata City Council legalized on-site smoking. On November 10, 2026, the Arcata Planning Commission unanimously approved an outdoor smoking lounge on our patio, for products bought in the store. The opening date and house rules haven't been published yet, and the store will post them when they're set.

Until then, our courtyard welcomes edibles and THC drinks. Read about [what to expect out back](/learn/courtyard-etiquette/), or visit the [courtyard lounge](/courtyard-lounge/) page.

## Our license and policies

Every licensed retailer has a state license number. Ours is C10-0001327-LIC, and it covers adult-use and medicinal retail. You can look up any California cannabis license through the Department of Cannabis Control.

Two store policies worth knowing: all sales include excise and sales tax, and we make no sales to parking lots, alleyways or other public areas.

## A quick checklist

- Bring a valid ID every time you shop.
- Stay within the possession limits.
- Keep purchases sealed, or in the trunk, while you drive.
- Enjoy cannabis at home or in a licensed consumption area, not in public.
- Store it safely, away from kids and pets.

## Questions?

Rules change, so check the [Department of Cannabis Control](https://cannabis.ca.gov/) for the latest. For questions about our shop, call 707-630-4098 or stop by 460 I St in Arcata.

glossary.def: Tetrahydrocannabinol, the main compound in cannabis that causes a high. Labels list it as a percentage for flower and concentrates, and in milligrams for edibles and drinks.
The raw, non-intoxicating form of THC found in the plant. Heat from a flame, a vape or an oven turns it into THC.
Cannabidiol, a cannabinoid that doesn't produce a high the way THC does. Many products pair it with THC, so check the ratio on the label.
Cannabinol, a cannabinoid that forms as THC ages. It often shows up in evening-themed products, though research on it is still limited.

Aromatic compounds that give cannabis its smell and flavor, from the same family found in citrus, pine and lavender. Many people believe they help shape the experience, though the research is still early.
A common terpene with an earthy, musky aroma, also found in hops and mango.
A terpene with a bright citrus aroma, also found in lemon and orange peel.
A terpene with a peppery, spicy aroma, also found in black pepper and cloves.
A terpene that smells like fresh pine needles, also found in rosemary.
A terpene with a soft floral aroma, best known from lavender.
A traditional label linked with a heavier, more relaxed feel. On our menu it lines up with Relax, as a loose guide rather than a promise.
A traditional label linked with a lighter, more upbeat feel. On our menu it lines up with Uplift, as a loose guide rather than a promise.
A cross of indica and sativa genetics, which covers most cannabis on shelves today. On our menu it lines up with Balance.
A specific variety of cannabis, like Blue Dream or GMO. Cultivar is the grower's word; strain is the everyday one.
A concentrate made from plants frozen fresh at harvest instead of dried and cured, to hold on to more of the fresh aroma.
A solventless concentrate pressed from flower or hash with heat and pressure. Live rosin starts with fresh-frozen plants.
A concentrate whipped to a soft, creamy texture, a bit like cake frosting. Sometimes spelled batter.
A runny, aromatic concentrate, often with THCA crystals mixed in.
Crystals of nearly pure THCA, often sold sitting in sauce. They're among the strongest products on the menu.
Resin glands (trichomes) collected from the plant and kept loose or pressed together. It's one of the oldest forms of cannabis concentrate.
A traditional, solventless hash made by sifting dried flower over fine screens to collect the resin glands.
A vape with the battery and the oil in one device, so there's nothing to match up.
The standard screw thread used by most vape cartridges and batteries, so a 510 cartridge fits most 510 batteries.
Flower that comes already rolled and ready to light. An infused pre-roll adds concentrate inside or on the outside, which makes it much stronger.
Cannabis grown outdoors under the sun, with no artificial light. It usually means one harvest a year, in the fall.
Cannabis grown in a greenhouse or hoop house using the sun plus some help, like blackout covers or extra lights.

Common flower weights: an eighth is 1/8 ounce (about 3.5 grams), a quarter is 1/4 ounce (about 7 grams), and zip is slang for a full ounce (about 28 grams). Zip is also a bag name on our menu and in our deals, so a Quarter Zip or a 1/4 oz Zip is 7 grams, not a full ounce.
The heating process that turns THCA into THC. It happens when you light or vape flower, and edible makers do it on purpose before infusing.
The theory that cannabinoids and terpenes work together to shape the experience, rather than THC alone. It's a popular idea, and the research is still developing.
Taking a very small amount of THC, often 2.5 mg or less, to keep effects light.

faq.q: Where is Humboldt's Premium Arcata?
faq.a: We're at 460 I St, Arcata, CA 95521, on the corner of I St. and Samoa Blvd. The Arcata Marsh is just south of us. Find a map on our [Visit page](/arcata-details/).

faq.q: What are your hours?
faq.a: Our posted hours are 9 am to 9 pm Monday through Saturday, and 10 am to 7 pm on Sunday. Hours can change, so check our [Visit page](/arcata-details/) or call 707-630-4098 before a special trip.

faq.q: What do I need to bring?
faq.a: A valid government-issued ID. You must be 21 or older, or 18 or older with a physician's recommendation if you're a medical patient. ID is required for every sale: no ID, no sale.

faq.q: Do you serve medical patients?
faq.a: Our state license covers both adult-use and medicinal retail. Under state law, medical patients 18 and over need a physician's recommendation. Call us at 707-630-4098 before your visit and we'll tell you what to bring.

faq.q: Do you have another location?
faq.a: Yes. Our sister store, Humboldt's Premium, is at 1131 Broadway in Eureka. You can reach them at 707-496-0506.

faq.q: What forms of payment do you take?
faq.a: Cash and debit. Debit has a $3.00 fee. Sorry, no credit.

faq.q: Is tax included?
faq.a: Our posted policy reads: "All Sales include excise and sales tax." If you'd like to check a total before you order, call us at 707-630-4098.

faq.q: Can I order ahead?
faq.a: Yes. Place an order online from our [Shop page](/shop/), or call it in at 707-630-4098, then pick it up in store. Bring your ID.

faq.q: What is your return and exchange policy?
faq.a: Our policy reads: "No refunds on any purchase. No exchanges after 72 hrs. from purchase, must have original product and packaging from purchase for exchange. Exchanges for defective/damaged products will be for same products only. Certain restrictions apply." Questions about a purchase? Call 707-630-4098.

faq.q: Do you have daily deals?
faq.a: Yes, there are deals every day of the week. See what's on today at [Deals](/deals/).

faq.q: Can I combine discounts?
faq.a: No. Discounts cannot be stacked or applied to items on special or to sale items.

faq.q: What is Spin the Wheel?
faq.a: On the 1st of every month, spend $50 or more and you get to spin the wheel. It includes both locations and delivery, while supplies last.

faq.q: Do you deliver?
faq.a: Yes. We offer delivery service from Trinidad to Rio Dell, including towns like Arcata, Eureka, McKinleyville, Blue Lake, Fortuna, Ferndale and Carlotta. To check your address, call 707-630-4098 or email delivery@humboldtafc.com. More on our [Delivery page](/delivery/).

faq.q: Is delivery free? Is there a minimum?
faq.a: Our site lists free home delivery. Minimums and delivery hours aren't posted, so call 707-630-4098 or email delivery@humboldtafc.com and we'll fill you in.

faq.q: Can you deliver to a parking lot or park?
faq.a: No. Our policy: no sales to parking lots or alleyways or other public areas. Have your ID ready when your order arrives.

faq.q: Can I consume in the courtyard?
faq.a: Today the courtyard welcomes edibles and THC drinks. It's non-smoking for now. See [what to expect out back](/learn/courtyard-etiquette/).

faq.q: When will the smoking lounge open?
faq.a: On November 10, 2026, the Arcata Planning Commission unanimously approved an outdoor smoking lounge on our patio. The opening date and house rules haven't been announced yet, and the store will post them when they're set. Keep an eye on our [courtyard lounge](/courtyard-lounge/) page.

faq.q: Can I bring my own products to the courtyard?
faq.a: We haven't published a policy on outside products. The city's approval for the smoking lounge covers products bought in the store, so plan on enjoying what you pick up here. If you're unsure, ask a budtender.

faq.q: What's the difference between indica, sativa and hybrid?
faq.a: They're traditional labels: indica is linked with a relaxing feel, sativa with an uplifting one, and hybrid sits in between. We use Relax, Balance and Uplift as a loose guide, but terpenes, cannabinoids and your own body matter more. Read [our guide](/learn/indica-sativa-hybrid/).

faq.q: Do you carry Humboldt-grown cannabis?
faq.a: Yes. Our [Humboldt Grown](/a-humboldt-grown/) category features local flower and prerolls. Learn [why Humboldt grown matters](/learn/humboldt-grown/).

faq.q: Do you sell CBD and CBN products?
faq.a: Yes. Find them in our [CBD/CBN](/a-cbd-cbn/), [tinctures](/a-tintctures/) and [topicals](/a-topicals/) categories. Many of these products also contain THC, so check the ratio on the label. More in [our CBD and CBN guide](/learn/cbd-and-cbn/).

faq.q: I'm new to edibles. Where should I start?
faq.a: Start low, go slow. Many first-timers start around 2.5 to 5 mg of THC and wait at least 2 hours before taking more. Effects vary by person and product. Our [edibles and drinks guide](/learn/edibles-and-drinks/) has more.
